lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Kitchen Care and Basic Food Safety
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: cross-contamination basics

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice cross-contamination basics. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: With a trusted adult, the learner practices the basics of avoiding cross-contamination by keeping raw-food-risk items (or an adult-designated stand-in) physically separate from ready-to-eat items, using separate cutting boards or containers and separate hand-washing breaks between handling each type, guided fully the first round and leading the second with adult confirmation.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult is present for the entire practice, both rounds.
Hands are washed between handling the raw-food-risk zone and the ready-to-eat zone every time.
Stop and ask for help if any raw-food-risk item's condition seems unusual.

simulationAlternative.description: If handling an actual raw-food-risk item isn't appropriate for this household, the learner instead uses two clearly labeled stand-in items (for example a red-tagged item representing 'raw' and a green-tagged item representing 'ready-to-eat') to practice the same two-zone separation and hand-washing breaks, with the adult confirming the zones stayed correctly separated.

materials: learner-local: two cutting boards or containers
adult-or-local: a raw-food-risk item or adult-designated stand-in

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u03-l03-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u03-l03-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u03-l03-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u03-l03-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain, in your own words, exactly what could go wrong if the two zones got mixed up — name a specific risk, not just 'it's unsafe.'

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u03-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Maintaining zone separation: Zones stay separate for the full guided round. | Explaining the risk: Names a plausible, specific risk of mixing zones. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Add a third zone (like a zone for washed produce) and have the learner reason through where it fits relative to the first two, explaining their placement to the adult.

resources.title: cross-contamination basics worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With a trusted adult, the learner practices the basics of avoiding cross-contamination by keeping raw-food-risk items (or an adult-designated stand-in) physically separate from ready-to-eat items, using separate cutting boards or containers and separate hand-washing breaks between handling each type, guided fully the first round and leading the second with adult confirmation.

resources.title: cross-contamination basics coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a trusted adult, the learner practices the basics of avoiding cross-contamination by keeping raw-food-risk items (or an adult-designated stand-in) physically separate from ready-to-eat items, using separate cutting boards or containers and separate hand-washing breaks between handling each type, guided fully the first round and leading the second with adult confirmation.
Coach direction: Before practicing, name one reason mixing a raw-food-risk item and a ready-to-eat item on the same surface could be a problem.
Learner prompt: Name one reason.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: cross-contamination basics complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult, set up two separate zones (or boards, or containers) — one for the raw-food-risk item, one for a ready-to-eat item — and practice moving between them correctly, washing hands between zones.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I used a separate surface or container for the raw-food-risk item the whole time.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I washed my hands after touching the raw-food-risk item and before touching the ready-to-eat item.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My adult confirmed the zones stayed separate throughout.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I did not set any ready-to-eat item down on a surface the raw-food-risk item had touched.

Equal-access rule: If handling an actual raw-food-risk item isn't appropriate for this household, the learner instead uses two clearly labeled stand-in items (for example a red-tagged item representing 'raw' and a green-tagged item representing 'ready-to-eat') to practice the same two-zone separation and hand-washing breaks, with the adult confirming the zones stayed correctly separated.

resources.title: cross-contamination basics minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain, in your own words, exactly what could go wrong if the two zones got mixed up — name a specific risk, not just 'it's unsafe.'
Success checks: Maintaining zone separation: Zones stay separate for the full guided round. | Explaining the risk: Names a plausible, specific risk of mixing zones.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: cross-contamination basics supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g5-u03-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional cross-contamination basics condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Maintaining zone separation: Zones stay separate for the full guided round. | Explaining the risk: Names a plausible, specific risk of mixing zones..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
